title: Platform team wiki: systems & services, dashboards, runbooks, retrospectives, and roadmap (Q1 2026)
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:

This page is the canonical platform team wiki for systems & services, dashboards and alerting, operational runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the near-term roadmap (Q1-Q2 2026). It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and on-call responders. Use this document as the first stop for: onboarding, runbook execution, dashboard maintenance, alert tuning, and planning work that impacts platform reliability and cost.

Table of contents:
1. Systems & services inventory
2. Dashboards and alerting (Grafana + Alertmanager + PagerDuty)
3. Runbooks (common incident types)
4. On-call and escalation matrix
5. Recent retrospectives (Q4 2025-Q1 2026)
6. Roadmap (Q1-Q2 2026)
7. How-tos and team wiki conventions
8. Owners and contacts

1) Systems & services inventory

Short intro: the platform team operates the following logical services. For each service we include: primary owner, SLOs, key metrics, and known operational patterns.

- service: platform-control-plane
  - owner: platform-control-team
  - SLOs: 99.95% availability across regions (p95 control-plane latency < 300ms)
  - key metrics: api.request_rate, api.5xx_rate, control_plane_cpu_util, etc.
  - common failure modes: DB connection storms after deploy, certificate rotation issues.

- service: ingress-router (kong / envoy mesh)
  - owner: edge-infra
  - SLOs: 99.99% request success for production routes, p95 latency < 40ms for health-check endpoints
  - key metrics: envoy.cluster_upstream_rq_5xx, kong.latency_p95, tls_handshake_errors
  - common failure modes: NLB target flapping, route misconfiguration, TLS expiry.

- service: request-batcher (continuous batching service for token-level optimization)
  - owner: serving-runtime
  - SLOs: 99.9% availability for batch window < 50ms, tail latency p99 < 500ms for interactive tier
  - key metrics: batch.size_histogram, batch.wait_ms, batch.latency_p99
  - common failure modes: threadpool starvation, backlog spikes after traffic bursts.

- service: kv-cache (redis-cluster w/ sentinel)
  - owner: platform-storage
  - SLOs: 99.95% availability, read latency p99 < 15ms
  - key metrics: redis.used_memory, redis.key_miss_rate, redis.latency_p99
  - common failure modes: eviction storms, replication lag after node restart

(Full inventory is maintained in the team wiki index: related_pages includes the systems playbook.)

2) Dashboards and alerting

Standard stack: Grafana for dashboards, Prometheus for metrics, Alertmanager for routing, PagerDuty for escalation. Dashboards follow a naming convention: platform.<service>.<view> (e.g., platform.kv-cache.overview).

High-priority dashboards to review during incident:
- platform.control-plane.overview
- platform.ingress-router.latency-and-errors
- platform.request-batcher.backpressure
- platform.gpu-fleet.capacity-utilization

Alerting policy (summary):
- Severity P0 (pager duty, phone, Slack #oncall-alerts): availability SLO breach, data-plane 5xx spike > 2% absolute for > 2m, controller leader eviction
- Severity P1 (pager duty, email, Slack): degradation of latency thresholds (p95 degrade > 2x baseline for > 5m), sustained resource exhaustion > 80% CPU on control-plane nodes
- Severity P2 (Slack + ticket): transient errors, elevated throttling, minor configuration drift

Recommended alert thresholds (examples):
| metric | threshold | severity | notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| api.5xx_rate | > 1% (prod) sustained 3m | P0 | Route to edge-infra & platform-control |
| kv-cache.replication_lag_ms | > 2000ms for 2m | P1 | Potential data loss risk if sustained |
| batch.wait_ms.p95 | > 120ms | P1 | Affects cost/latency tradeoffs |
| node.cpu_usage | > 85% sustained 5m | P1 | Scale or investigate runaway processes |

Alert routing and silencing:
- PagerDuty services by owner team (e.g., platform-control-plane-pd, serving-runtime-pd).
- Use Alertmanager silences for planned maintenance; silences must include a runbook link and a CI-run incident tag.

3) Runbooks (common incident types)

Runbook: Control-plane high error rate (api.5xx_rate > 1% sustained)
Steps:
1. Triage: Check platform.control-plane.overview dashboard (top 5 erroring endpoints) and the most recent deploys (CI pipeline ID).
2. Determine scope: query logs for X-Request-ID to see if errors are universal or single-route.
3. If caused by recent deploy: rollback using the deployment pipeline (link in team wiki). Notify release owner and open a postmortem if outage > 5 min.
4. If caused by DB connection saturation: check connection pool usage, increase pool limits, restart workers systematically (1 zone at a time).
5. If unresolved after 10m: escalate to platform-control-plane-oncall -> engage DB infra and SRE.
6. Post-incident: run the regression-triage checklist and attach affected prompts/eval sets to release notes.

Runbook: GPU fleet node unavailable / scheduling failures
Steps:
1. Check gpu-fleet.capacity-utilization dashboard and node exporter metrics (gpu.temp, gpu.mem_used).
2. If node health failing: cordon node, drain workloads and replace via autoscaler (terraform apply module.gpu_autoscaler).
3. If scheduling failures are widespread: check kube-scheduler logs, leader status, and etcd health.
4. Notify serving-runtime owners and engage cloud-provider support if underlying host is unhealthy.

Runbook: KV-cache eviction storm
Steps:
1. Inspect redis.metrics (used_memory, evicted_keys). Determine if a bad key pattern is causing hot key churn.
2. If hot key identified: add temporary rate limit at application proxy and create a mitigation request to the service owner.
3. Restore cache by warming critical keys via job; consider adding a read-through fallback to persistent store.

4) On-call and escalation matrix

- Primary on-call (platform): 24/7 rotation, ROTA length: 7 days
- Secondary on-call: handles escalations during business hours and provides second-tier support
- Escalation order: primary -> secondary -> team lead -> SRE director -> PagerDuty global rotation
- Contact policy: phone for P0, Slack for P1, ticket for P2

5) Recent retrospectives (Q4 2025-Q1 2026)

Summary of major incidents and key improvements:
- Incident: control-plane outage (2025-11-17) caused by DB migration locking; impact: 22m total and 11m degraded.
  - Action items: introduce online-safe migrations (feature-flagged), add pre-migration load test, enforce deploy freeze for control-plane migrations.
  - Status: migrations playbook merged (PR #452), added pre-migration checklist to CI.

- Incident: large request-batcher backlog after a marketing traffic spike (2026-01-09).
  - Root cause: unbounded client that sent large prefix-heavy requests; batcher backpressure not tuned for this pattern.
  - Action items: add protective rate-limiter per ingress-token, improve batch.wait_ms autoscaling, add a new dashboard panel for prefix-distribution.
  - Status: rate-limiter merged and in canary, batch autoscaler tuning scheduled for Feb 2026 sprint.

Lessons learned (cross-cutting):
- Add more synthetic canaries that test high-cardinality prompt patterns.
- Make rollback faster by simplifying the deployment graph for critical control-plane services.
- Ensure runbooks include exact CLI commands and CI pipeline IDs where possible.

6) Roadmap (Q1-Q2 2026)

Planned initiatives and owners (quarterly priorities):
- Q1 2026: Observability modernization (owner: platform-observability)
  - Migrate dashboards to Grafana v9, standardize panel templates, add cost-by-route metric, improve tagging to support multi-tenancy filtering.
  - Deliverables: new dashboard templates, migration guide, training sessions (Mar 2026).

- Q1 2026: Runbook hardening and automation (owner: platform-ops)
  - Convert top-10 runbooks to automated playbooks (runbook-automation repo), add one-click remediation actions (scale up/down, rollback).
  - Deliverables: 5 automated runbooks, CI gating for runbook changes.

- Q2 2026: Capacity planning & cost controls (owner: eng-sre)
  - Implement predictive autoscaling for GPU pools, integrate cost alerts, and publish quarterly capacity report.
  - Deliverables: predictive model prototype, cost alert thresholds, capacity report template.

- Q2 2026: Platform team wiki consolidation (owner: platform-knowledge)
  - Consolidate duplicate docs, add templates for dashboards/runbooks, and maintain a living inventory for services.

Roadmap timeline (high-level):
- Feb 2026: runbook automation MVP
- Mar 2026: Grafana migration and dashboard templates
- Apr-May 2026: predictive GPU autoscaling pilot
- Jun 2026: capacity & cost report; documentation consolidation complete

7) How-tos and team wiki conventions

Confluence structure and conventions:
- Page titles: use kebab-case when exporting JSON (e.g., platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-q1-2026).
- Dashboards: include "owner" and "last_reviewed" annotation on the dashboard description (e.g., owner: @Daniel Kim, last_reviewed: 2026-01-12).
- Runbooks: include a short summary, pre-req checks, step-by-step remediation, escalation links, and postmortem checklist. Each runbook must reference a CI pipeline or link to the code deploy artifact.
- Labels: use one of the labels listed at the top of this page. Keep label list to < 8 tags.

How to add a new dashboard (quick steps):
1. Create a new Grafana panel following the platform.<service>.<view> naming convention.
2. Add owner and last_reviewed annotation in the panel description.
3. Save to the platform team folder and create a PR against grafana-as-code repo. Include screenshots and acceptance criteria.
4. After merge, update the runbook and add an alert rule if the panel exposes user-impacting metrics.

How to tune alerts safely:
1. Default to conservative thresholds; validate against 90 days of historical data.
2. Add a `:test` route and run simulated load to validate firing conditions.
3. When lowering severity, document rationale in the alert rule and add a reviewer.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets

- Rollback last deploy (example):
  - ci rollback --pipeline platform-control-plane --to=last-stable 

- Cordon and drain a GPU node: 
  - kubectl cordon <node-name>
  - kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

- Create an Alertmanager silence (example):
  - curl -XPOST -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"HighCPU","isRegex":false}],"startsAt":"2026-02-20T15:00:00Z","endsAt":"2026-02-20T17:00:00Z","createdBy":"platform-oncall","comment":"Planned maintenance"}' https://alertmanager.internal/api/v1/silences

Document maintenance:
- Owners must review this page quarterly. After incidents or significant changes, update the runbooks and last_reviewed annotations on relevant dashboards.

End of document.
